takeaways: Motion triggered by interaction — parallax, zooms, big slides — can cause dizziness, nausea and migraines.
Respect the system “Reduce motion” setting. Developers read it as prefers-reduced-motion.
Swap travel for fades or instant changes. Keep the feedback; lose the movement.
It’s Level AAA, but because every OS exposes the setting, it’s one of the easiest AAA wins.
failures: Scroll-driven parallax with no off switch
Backgrounds that shift as you scroll
check: Turn on Reduce motion on your device and walk through the prototype.
Spec a reduced alternative for every animation at handoff.
Ask of each animation: is it essential, or decoration?

quiz.question: Your onboarding uses heavy parallax as people scroll. What does 2.3.3 ask for?
options: A way to turn that motion off
quiz.why: Most people can keep the motion — but those affected need to turn it off, for example by honoring Reduce motion.

spec: For every animation, specify a reduced version: a fade, or no transition.
Mark which motion is essential to understanding, and why.
Reference the system setting so developers wire up prefers-reduced-motion.
review: What does this flow look like with Reduce motion on?
Which animation here is decoration, and which carries meaning?
Does anything move without the person triggering it? That is 2.2.2.
tradeoff: Motion is part of the brand. Reduced does not mean none: keep opacity and color changes, drop travel, scale and parallax.
system: Give every motion token a reduced value, so each component gets the alternative for free.
pitch: The setting already exists on every device and people already use it. Ignoring it means making some customers feel ill.
